assessments.evidence: The tawny dark-maned lion visibly splits the enemy mass and Devi's noose visibly binds near attackers while authorized weapons hold the center. The locked final beat is absent: no breath, vapor or luminous exhalation leaves Devi, so the required transition into page 14 is not present.

The visible discus, conch, lotus, mace, trident/spear, bow and noose are all within the authorized equipment list, and the many-armed identity is readable. A complete luminous disk nevertheless sits behind Devi's head, contrary to the character bible's prohibition on unsourced halo symbolism; no qualified theological approval is being inferred.

The principal figures, dress and equipment use a coherent Indian visual vocabulary and avoid Western armor, but an elaborate palace-temple complex appears on the distant right. The battlefield location bible specifies a ridge and action lanes, not a palace, and explicitly prohibits geographic overclaim.

This panel presents an explicit eight-arm, fully equipped Devi with a pink-white garland, while the immediately preceding panel presents a sparse weaponless arm field with a white garland and different halo/crown construction. The lion itself matches the tawny-gold, dark-maned bible proposal.

The lion charge and noose capture are immediately clear at reading size, but the intended final transition cannot be read because Devi shows no visible exhalation. The panel therefore ends on battle action rather than the specified breath cue.

At 1536x1024 the lion's anatomy, Devi's face and visible hands, rope loops, foreground soldiers and depth remain crisp. The action has strong focal hierarchy and no decisive fused face, malformed hand, detached limb or raster artifact.

No raster text, logo or watermark is present. A broad low-detail blue-sky field across the upper center and right remains available for a narration plaque without covering Devi's face, the lion, the noose or the bound attackers.

The lower camera, lunging lion and foreground attackers create distinct action lanes; the noose lines lead from Devi to the caught soldiers, and the mountain ridge preserves depth. The central action remains readable at page size.
The output uses Reference A's devotional finish and Reference B's battle depth and sequential clarity without copying Raktabija, blood effects, flags, Western-fantasy armor or DM08 story action.
